content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text addresses Matthew 1:20 as a cited verse and says both sides answered it, so it decides whether to treat it as an unanswered witness.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.","room":"The phrase 'counts as an unanswered witness' could be read as treating UNDERDETERMINED as still counting Matthew 1:20 as unanswered, but the better reading is that because the judge expressly says both sides answered, it is not counting it as unanswered.","why":"The judge text says the verse was answered by the challenger and defender and does not count it as an unanswered witness, so it obeys K-G4."}
